title: SHAPE-Seq
scope: Lucks 2011 SHAPE-Seq implementation; stop-based readout rather than automatically importing mutational profiling. Extraction covers the assigned RNA-to-cDNA schematic and the matching SHAPE-Seq row of the supplied poster. The left RNA icon expands the assay name rather than depicting an additional treatment. The two marked molecules illustrate different modification positions and separately drawn product histories, without establishing isolated fractions. The schematic ends at physical cDNA; the catalogue description and primary abstract explain the downstream sequencing readout without supplying unshown library-preparation operations.

operations.label: Hydrolyze RNA in the upper RNA/cDNA product
operations.description: RNA hydrolysis removes the template from the upper illustrated RNA/cDNA product, leaving its longer cDNA product, drawn as a blue line.
operations.mechanism: The RNA strand is hydrolyzed; cDNA is retained. No conditions, work-up, or additional library construction are specified.
operations.information_effect: The RNA and its modification cease to be the depicted product; the cDNA endpoint preserves the positional surrogate. The primary abstract identifies paired-end deep sequencing of primer-extension products as the readout. Neither sequencing nor the intervening construction of a sequencing-ready library is drawn here. Stop-derived structure inference requires the catalogue-described controls for transcriptase drop-off, and the in vitro fold may differ from the in vivo fold. Across many primer-extension products, the stop-position distribution supplies the single-nucleotide structural information described by the sources; an individual stop alone does not establish a complete RNA structure.

operations.label: Hydrolyze RNA in the lower RNA/cDNA product
operations.description: RNA hydrolysis removes the template from the lower illustrated RNA/cDNA product, leaving its shorter cDNA product, drawn as a blue line.
operations.mechanism: The RNA strand is hydrolyzed; cDNA is retained. No conditions, work-up, or additional library construction are specified.
operations.information_effect: The RNA and its modification cease to be the depicted product; the cDNA endpoint preserves the positional surrogate. The primary abstract identifies paired-end deep sequencing of primer-extension products as the readout. Neither sequencing nor the intervening construction of a sequencing-ready library is drawn here. Stop-derived structure inference requires the catalogue-described controls for transcriptase drop-off, and the in vitro fold may differ from the in vivo fold. Across many primer-extension products, the stop-position distribution supplies the single-nucleotide structural information described by the sources; an individual stop alone does not establish a complete RNA structure.

Primary full text is unavailable in the registry, so this does not establish that all complete SHAPE-Seq implementations share an identical experimental recipe.
